nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. Two simplex vertices $s$ and $t$ of $G$ are adjacent in the simplex graph of $G$ if and only if their symmetric difference $s \triangle t$ has exactly one element.
nodes.title: Adjacency in the simplex graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. For every vertex $v$ of $G$, the empty simplex vertex of $G$ and the singleton simplex vertex of $v$ are adjacent in the simplex graph of $G$.
nodes.title: The empty clique is adjacent to every singleton

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. The empty simplex vertex of $G$ is the empty set of vertices, which is a clique of $G$.
nodes.title: Empty simplex vertex

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. The simplex graph of $G$ is the simple graph whose vertices are the simplex vertices of $G$ (the finite cliques of $G$), in which two cliques $s$ and $t$ are adjacent exactly when their symmetric difference $s \triangle t$ has exactly one element.
nodes.title: Simplex graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex type $V$. A simplex vertex of $G$ is a finite set $s$ of vertices that is a clique of $G$, meaning that any two distinct elements of $s$ are adjacent in $G$.
nodes.title: Simplex vertices

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. For a vertex $v$ of $G$, the singleton simplex vertex of $v$ is the one-element set containing $v$, which is a clique of $G$.
nodes.title: Singleton simplex vertex

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
